sections.title: The Resurrection of Jesus
observations: This section describes the discovery of the empty tomb by Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome. Their visit to the tomb signifies the importance of women in the resurrection narrative, as they are the first witnesses to the resurrection.
The angel's message to the women emphasizes the fulfillment of Jesus' predictions about His resurrection, providing a foundation for the Christian faith.

sections.title: The Great Commission
observations: After appearing to Mary Magdalene, Jesus commissions His disciples to spread the gospel to all creation. This marks a pivotal moment in the establishment of the church and the mission of believers.
The command to baptize and teach underscores the importance of discipleship and the continuation of Jesus' ministry through His followers.

importantVerses.commentary: The angel's proclamation of Jesus' resurrection is central to the Christian faith, affirming that He has risen and is not in the tomb.
The Great Commission is a foundational verse for evangelism and mission work, highlighting the responsibility of believers to share the gospel.

questions: What does the resurrection of Jesus mean for believers today?
How does the role of women in the resurrection narrative challenge or affirm traditional views of gender in ministry?
What implications does the Great Commission have for the church's mission in the modern world?
